name: Problem / rozwiązanie
description: Gdy oferta odpowiada na łatwo rozpoznawalny problem.
rules: Use a real audience problem.
Include up to three supported offer details with audience benefits.
Use trust proof only when verified; otherwise close with the CTA.

structure.name: Problem hook
structure.purpose: Name a concrete everyday problem in an engaging first line.

structure.name: Solution
structure.purpose: Introduce the offer as a relevant solution.

structure.name: Offer details and benefits
structure.purpose: Show up to three verified features, service elements or terms and what each gives the audience.

structure.name: Offer
structure.purpose: Present the actual offer without inventing a promotion.

structure.name: Trust or CTA
structure.purpose: Add verified proof if available, then invite the reader to act.

name: Klasyczne ad copy
description: Dla oferty z konkretnym sposobem działania lub realizacji.
rules: Promise only a plausible, supported result.
Explain how the offer works or is delivered when known rather than relying on generic slogans.

structure.name: Result
structure.purpose: Open with a concrete, credible desired result.

structure.name: Offer and mechanism
structure.purpose: Introduce the offer and explain how it works or is delivered when known.

structure.name: Main benefits
structure.purpose: Show the strongest customer benefits.

structure.name: Convenience
structure.purpose: Add a supported convenience benefit if relevant.

structure.name: CTA
structure.purpose: Invite the reader to take the next step appropriate to the offer.

name: Benefity w punktach (master)
rules: Write up to three distinct, supported USP or benefits, each on its own line starting with '- '.
Do not list offer details without explaining audience value.

structure.name: Hook
structure.purpose: Use a short, engaging first line.

structure.name: Benefits
structure.purpose: Write up to three strongest supported benefits as separate bullet points.

structure.name: Positive result
structure.purpose: Show a realistic customer outcome supported by those benefits.

structure.name: Offer or CTA
structure.purpose: Present a real offer if available; otherwise use a neutral CTA.

name: Storytelling / opinia
description: Historia klienta albo uczciwa narracja marki.
rules: Never invent a customer, quote, testimonial or personal experience.
Without an authentic customer story, use a brand narrative without pretending it is a review.

structure.name: Story
structure.purpose: Begin with a real customer story or a clearly brand-led scene.

structure.name: Difficulty
structure.purpose: Show the earlier difficulty without exaggeration.

structure.name: Discovery
structure.purpose: Introduce the offer as a relevant option.

structure.name: Experience
structure.purpose: Describe only documented experience or a factual offer benefit.

structure.name: CTA
structure.purpose: Invite the reader to learn more.

name: Pytanie-zaczepka
rules: Ask about a situation, not the reader's sensitive attributes or medical condition.
Use up to three distinct, supported benefits.

structure.name: Question
structure.purpose: Ask an intriguing, relevant question.

structure.name: Situation
structure.purpose: Describe a familiar situation.

structure.name: Solution
structure.purpose: Introduce the offer as a relevant answer.

structure.name: Benefits
structure.purpose: Present up to three supported practical customer benefits.

structure.name: Offer
structure.purpose: Present the actual offer without invented urgency.

structure.name: CTA
structure.purpose: Invite the reader to take the next step.

name: Idealny świat vs rzeczywistość
description: Kontrast dla codziennej wygody i stylu życia.
rules: Keep the ideal scenario plausible.
Describe only problems and benefits grounded in the supplied data.

structure.name: Ideal scene
structure.purpose: Describe a desirable everyday situation.

structure.name: Reality
structure.purpose: Contrast it with a real friction point.

structure.name: Bridge
structure.purpose: Show how the offer helps bridge the gap.

structure.name: Benefits
structure.purpose: Name the most relevant practical benefits.

structure.name: Offer
structure.purpose: Present the actual offer.

structure.name: CTA
structure.purpose: Invite the reader to take the next step appropriate to the offer.

name: Przeszłość vs przyszłość
rules: Do not promise guaranteed transformation or an unsupported result.

structure.name: Before
structure.purpose: Describe the present or previous situation.

structure.name: After
structure.purpose: Show a credible improved situation.

structure.name: Bridge
structure.purpose: Introduce the offer as a way to help make that change.

structure.name: Benefits
structure.purpose: Show the supported benefits that explain the change.

structure.name: CTA
structure.purpose: Invite the reader to take action.

name: AIDA
rules: Build interest and desire from real offer value, not hype.

structure.name: Attention
structure.purpose: Catch attention with a specific hook.

structure.name: Interest
structure.purpose: Explain why this offer is relevant.

structure.name: Desire
structure.purpose: Show a credible customer benefit.

structure.name: Action
structure.purpose: Give a clear next step.

name: PAS
rules: Do not use fear, shame or exaggerated consequences.
End the solution with a natural next step when allowed by the instructions.

structure.name: Problem
structure.purpose: Name a concrete customer problem.

structure.name: Agitation
structure.purpose: Explain the ordinary inconvenience it causes without dramatizing.

structure.name: Solution
structure.purpose: Show how the offer helps and invite the reader to learn more.

name: BAB
rules: Describe the after state as a plausible benefit, not a guaranteed result.

structure.name: Before
structure.purpose: Describe the initial situation.

structure.name: After
structure.purpose: Show the credible desired situation.

structure.name: Bridge
structure.purpose: Explain how the offer helps connect the two and suggest an appropriate next step.

name: FAB
rules: Connect one real offer feature, service element or term to its practical advantage and audience benefit.

structure.name: Feature
structure.purpose: Introduce a verified feature, service element or offer term.

structure.name: Advantage
structure.purpose: Explain what that feature makes easier or different.

structure.name: Benefit
structure.purpose: Show what the customer gains and a natural next step.

name: 4P
rules: Use only a credible, supported promise.
Use a real proof point when available; otherwise ground this step in a verifiable offer fact. Never invent evidence.

structure.name: Picture
structure.purpose: Show a relevant positive vision.

structure.name: Promise
structure.purpose: Describe a supported offer benefit.

structure.name: Prove
structure.purpose: Use a real fact, demonstration or verified evidence.

structure.name: Push
structure.purpose: Invite the reader to act.

name: Offer first
rules: Use a special promotion only if it really exists; otherwise lead with the ordinary offer.

structure.name: Offer hook
structure.purpose: Open with the actual offer or value proposition.

structure.name: Value
structure.purpose: Explain what the offer includes and why it matters.

structure.name: Benefits
structure.purpose: Give two or three supported customer benefits.

structure.name: CTA
structure.purpose: Invite the reader to take the next step appropriate to the offer.

name: Objection handling
description: Odpowiada na konkretną wątpliwość odbiorcy oferty.
rules: Use only an objection supported by the supplied context or a clearly framed common question.
Answer factually; do not invent guarantees or policy terms.

structure.name: Objection
structure.purpose: State a relevant customer question or doubt.

structure.name: Answer
structure.purpose: Give a specific, factual answer.

structure.name: Confirmation
structure.purpose: Support the answer with a real feature or evidence.

structure.name: CTA
structure.purpose: Invite the reader to learn more.

name: Comparison
rules: Use only a documented, specific difference.
Do not make unsupported claims about competitors or name them without reliable evidence.

structure.name: Typical option
structure.purpose: Describe a common alternative without disparagement.

structure.name: Offer
structure.purpose: Introduce what is actually offered.

structure.name: Difference
structure.purpose: Explain a documented difference.

structure.name: Benefit
structure.purpose: Show what that difference means for the customer.

structure.name: CTA
structure.purpose: Invite the reader to compare or learn more.
